Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public. 




Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan 
"The Right to Information, The Right to Live"

Indian Standard (Reaffirmed 1998) 
SPECIFICATION FOR 
GAG, MOUTH, MASON'S PATTERN 



1. Scope — Covers dimensional and other requirements for Mason's pattern mouth gag, used fn 
resuscitation, oral surgery and anaesthesia. 



2. Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. 1.

IS: 7627- 1975 

2.1 A deviation of ± 2*5 percent shall be allowed on all dimensions. 

3. Material— Stainless steel bars conforming to Designation 22Cr1 3 or 30Cr13 of IS: 6603-1972 
' Specification for stainless steel bars and flats '. 

4. Workmanship and Finish 

4.1 The gag shall be free from rough edges, pits, cracks, burrs, seams and other surface defects, 

4.2 All edges shall be smooth and even. The serrations and knurling, wherever provided, shall be 
well-formed and clean. 

4.3 The handle portion shall have serrations or grooves for proper grip. 

4.4 The joints shall work smoothly and shall not have any undue play. 

4.5 The gag shall be polished bright and passivated. 

5. Heat Treatment — The gag shall be hardened and tempered to give a hardness of 430 to 490 HV* 

6. Tests 

6.1 Flexibility Test — Lock the two arms of the gag in its fully opened position. Apply a compressive 
force of 400 N at the top of the arms in such a manner that it acts at the centre of the arms. Attain 
the force gradually and apply for two minutes. On completion of the test, the mouth gag shall not 
show any sign of damage. 

6.2 Corrosion Resistance Test — Scrub the sample with soap and warm water, rinse in hot water and 
then dip in 95 percent ethyl alcohol. Dry the sample. Immerse in copper sulphate solution at room 
temperature for 6 minutes and then wash off with fresh water or wet cotton wool. 

Composition of the solution shall be as follows: 

Copper sulphate ( CuS0 4 .5H 2 ) 4*0 g 

Sulphuric acid ( H 2 S0 4 ) ( sp gr V84) 10"0g 

Distilled water [ see IS : 1 070-1 960 Specification for 900 ml 

water, distilled quality ( revised ) ]. 

There shall be no red stains or spots on the sample but dulling of the polished surface may be 
permitted. 

7. Marking — The gag shall be marked with manufacturer's name, initials or recognized trade-mark. 
7.1 ISI Certification Marking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

8. Packing — As agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer. 



Printed at Delhi Printers, Delhi, India
